property_summary: For any sequence of Put and Collect calls, the contract balance of C equals the sum of all user balances recorded in Acc, which the mutant violates by subtracting msg.value on Put instead of adding it.
After a Put and a successful Collect after unlock, the sum of user balances equals the contract balance; the mutant violates this because Put subtracts instead of adds.

After a Put followed by any number of Collects where sum of successful collects <= sent value, the user's Acc balance plus total successfully collected is equal to the initially deposited value; the mutant violates this because Put subtracts instead of adding.

For any address, after any sequence of self-callable Put and Collect operations, the Acc mapping balance is never negative (i.e., it never underflows); the buggy version decreases balance on Put instead of increasing it, causing an underflow on Collect for some input.

Correct C puts the unlockTime for the caller which must be >= block.timestamp; the mutant skips updating it so the stored unlockTime stays at 0, violating the invariant that Acc[caller].unlockTime >= block.timestamp after a Put.

After any call to Put, the caller's unlockTime must equal the maximum of the passed _unlockTime and block.timestamp; the mutant never updates unlockTime so it remains 0, violating this invariant for any non-zero future unlock time.
After a call to Put with a future _unlockTime, the caller's unlockTime in the reference is strictly greater than the block.timestamp at the time of the call, while the mutant leaves it at 0.

After a call to Put with a specific _unlockTime, the caller's unlockTime must equal _unlockTime if _unlockTime > block.timestamp, otherwise equal block.timestamp; the mutant leaves it at 0, violating this equality.

After a call to Put with a future _unlockTime, the sender's unlockTime in the reference will be at least block.timestamp at the time of the call, while the mutant leaves it uninitialized at 0, making it possible to immediately call Collect by warping past the unlockTime.
For any caller, after Put is invoked, the caller's recorded balance in Acc must equal the value sent with the call; the buggy version always sets it to zero, breaking this rule.
For any caller, after Put is invoked, Acc[msg.sender].balance must be greater than or equal to msg.value; the buggy version sets it to zero, violating this rule when msg.value > 0.

For any caller and any msg.value, after Put, Acc[msg.sender].balance must equal the sum of previous balance and msg.value; the bug sets balance to 0, breaking the invariant when msg.value > 0 or previous balance > 0.
After any sequence of Put calls, for each caller the stored balance must be at least the sum of msg.value sent; the bug sets balance to 0, violating this when any caller sends >0.
After any call to Put, the acc.unlockTime for the caller must be strictly greater than the previous block.timestamp (or zero), but the mutant sets it to zero, allowing premature collection.

For any sender, after a call to Put with a non-zero _unlockTime > block.timestamp, the sender's unlockTime must be strictly greater than block.timestamp at the time of the call; the mutant sets it to zero, so a subsequent Collect can succeed even though block.timestamp has not exceeded the intended unlockTime.
After any Put call, the caller's unlockTime should be at least block.timestamp; the mutant sets it to 0, so a subsequent Collect can succeed before block.timestamp > 0 elapses.

For any sender who calls Put with an unlockTime > block.timestamp, that sender's Acc.unlockTime must be >= the passed _unlockTime parameter; the mutant sets it to 0, so for any non-zero _unlockTime the property is violated.

For any sender, after a call to the public Put function with any arguments, the sender's unlockTime must never decrease; the mutant forces it to zero, so a subsequent Put with a non-zero _unlockTime will violate this non-decreasing invariant.

A re-entrant caller must not be able to increase their balance more than msg.value during a single Put, but removing the nonReentrant check lets a re-entrant caller drain more than msg.value by calling Collect inside Put's external call via fallback.

After any external call from Put completes, the balance of the caller must equal the sum of their prior balance and the msg.value sent, but the mutant allows a re-entrant Collect to reduce the balance before Put's addition, violating this invariant.
During an external call from Put, re-entrant Collect can change the caller's balance, so after Put completes the caller's balance is no longer equal to the sum of their pre-put balance and msg.value.

After any external call from Put completes, the contract's locked_ variable must be false; in the mutant, a re-entrant Collect call during Put's external call leaves locked_ true when the base Put completes, violating this invariant.

After any call to Put(msg.value) from an EOA, the caller's Acc balance must be at least msg.value greater than before the call; the bug allows a re-entrant Collect via a fallback to steal the msg.value before Put adds it.

After any number of Put calls, the user's account balance (Acc[user].balance) must equal the total Ether they contributed; the bug breaks this because the modifier reentrancy lock never releases, so after the first Put, any subsequent Put reverts.

After any number of Put calls by a single user, the contract's internal balance for that user (`Acc[user].balance`) must equal the user's total contributions; the bug prevents any contribution after the first because the reentrancy lock never releases, causing subsequent Put calls to revert and the balance to be strictly less than the total sent.
